title: Momentum-resolved thermodynamics and barrier-free order-parameter collapse in spin-orbit-coupled superconductors under a Zeeman field
authors: Xusheng Wang, Gaomin Tang, Lianyi He, Shuai-Hua Ji
abstract: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) can enhance the critical Zeeman field of clean superconductors beyond the Pauli limit. We develop a momentum decomposition of the zero-temperature free energy to investigate spin-singlet $s$-wave superconductors with general time-reversal-symmetric SOC. The SOC component perpendicular to the Zeeman field enhances the critical field and suppresses first-order features, whereas the parallel component favors Pauli-limited thermodynamic behavior. Applying this framework to Rashba superconductors and Ising superconductors with weak Rashba SOC, we identify the origin of the abrupt collapse of the superconducting order parameter at the critical field. Competing angular contributions produce a nearly flat free-energy landscape, allowing a barrier-free order-parameter collapse distinct from the conventional Pauli-limited first-order transition.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes how spin-orbit coupling modifies the superconducting phase transition in superconductors under a magnetic field. By decomposing the free energy based on momentum, the authors show that the order parameter collapses without the typical energy barrier when competing angular contributions cancel out. This mechanism provides a novel understanding of superconducting critical fields beyond simple Pauli limiting.
main_problem: The study investigates the momentum-resolved thermodynamics and the nature of the superconducting order-parameter collapse in spin-orbit-coupled superconductors subjected to an external Zeeman field.
main_result: The abrupt collapse of the superconducting order parameter occurs due to the cancellation of competing angular contributions in the free energy, resulting in a barrier-free transition distinct from conventional first-order Pauli-limited transitions.
method: The authors employ a momentum decomposition of the zero-temperature free energy, analyzing angular contributions derived from the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The model considers spin-singlet s-wave superconductors with general time-reversal-symmetric Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC), specifically applying the framework to Rashba and Ising superconductors.
key_observables: Critical Zeeman field ($h_c$), potential barrier height ($P_B$), and the superconducting order parameter ($\Delta$) as a function of the magnetic field.
important_parameters: SOC strength ($\alpha_{SO}$), Zeeman field magnitude ($h$), and the relative orientation ($\varphi$) between the SOC vector and the Zeeman field.
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the zero-temperature limit, and for 2D systems, the SOC vector is approximated as being evaluated on the Fermi surface ($\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{p}) \simeq \mathbf{g}(	heta)$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how $h_c$ and $P_B$ vary with SOC orientation and strength, and show free-energy landscapes confirming the barrier-free collapse mechanism in both Rashba and Ising systems.
paper_structure: The paper develops the momentum-resolved free energy formalism, analyzes the SOC orientation dependence ($\phi$ dependence), and applies this framework to specific models (Rashba and Ising) to pinpoint the mechanism causing the barrier-free order parameter collapse.
why_interesting: The concept of a barrier-free phase transition driven by competing angular contributions in the free energy landscape is a sophisticated many-body phenomenon relevant to understanding exotic superconducting phase transitions.
